about: DestructiveConfirm — a pause before an action that cannot be undone. An alert dialog: the title is a question, the consequence is read with it, Cancel comes first and takes focus, the action is the da

title.about: A question with the action's words: "Delete project?". Never "Are you sure?".

consequence.about: What will happen, naming the thing: "You're deleting acme-web. You cannot undo this action." Read when it opens.

confirmLabel.about: The action in the title's words: "Delete project", never "OK".

cancelLabel.about: "Cancel", or "Keep [thing]" when the action is itself a cancellation.

severity.about: medium: confirm with a button. high (it takes other things with it, or cannot be put back): type the thing's name first. Low needs no dialog: do it, and offer Undo in a Toast.

confirmText.about: The name to type, for high.

confirmPrompt.about: The label of the field for high. Defaults to "Enter [name] to confirm".

onConfirm.about: The action. The dialog stays open and busy until it settles, and shows the error if it fails.

returnFocusTo.about: Where focus goes on close when the thing (and the button that opened this) is gone.

pairWith.DestructiveConfirm.Show name field: confirmText (omit it to hide the typed confirmation)
